verdict.rationale: MotherDuck documents a local-first dev loop: you develop and iterate locally on DuckDB, queries route between local and cloud, and a dbt project moves to MotherDuck by changing only the `path:` setting. A no-credit-card Lite plan with free storage and compute covers free cloud dev, and a community comment welcomes the hybrid local/remote execution. Missing for 10: an explicit documented dev-to-prod target workflow for transformations, and hands-on corroboration of the local dbt iteration loop.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I get a fast local or free dev loop — a local engine, emulator, or sandbox — to develop transformations before touching production compute

citations.quote: Develop and iterate locally, then share and scale in the cloud when you need it.
Queries are automatically routed to the optimal location: local DuckDB, MotherDuck cloud, or both
The only change needed for motherduck is the `path:` setting.
you can continue with the Lite plan (no credit card required)
dbt-duckdb is the adapter which allows dbt to use DuckDB and MotherDuck.
